about: Grand-Puy-Lacoste is a Fifth Growth of the 1855 Classification, named for the gravel “puys,” or hills, behind the town of Pauillac and for the Lacoste family, who owned it from the early 1700s to the late 1800s. The Borie family took over in 1978, and François-Xavier Borie has made the wine since 1979, becoming owner in 2003 and renovating the cellars from 2004. His children, Emeline and Pierre-Antoine, now share the running of the estate.

The vines grow in one block around the château, on deep gravel, pebbles and stones over limestone, planted mostly to Cabernet Sauvignon with Merlot and a little Cabernet Franc. The grapes are picked by hand and fermented parcel by parcel in temperature-controlled stainless steel vats, with malolactic fermentation in tank, before the wine ages for 16 to 18 months in French oak barrels. The 2010 is built mainly on Cabernet Sauvignon, which gives the wine its cassis fruit and firm frame.

2010 was a great, structured Bordeaux vintage, and many consider it, alongside 2009, among the finest wines the estate has made. Robert Parker called it the greatest Grand-Puy-Lacoste since 2005, 2000 and 1990, describing crème de cassis, blackberries, crushed rock and flowers over sweet tannins. Now past its fifteenth year, it is entering the window when classic Pauillac shows both its fruit and the cedar and tobacco notes that come with age.
facts: Single block on deep gravel over limestone; 10,000 vines per hectare
